All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.2.1] - 2026-09-29

### Changed

- Published to PyPI (`pip install astromesh-prisma`), with a project description, links to the
  docs and an sdist limited to the package, its tests and the license.

### Fixed

- The README started `api.main:create_app`, an app with no reconciler, where `/v1/translate`
  and `/reconcile` do not exist; it now starts `astromesh_prisma.app:app`, as the Dockerfile does.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-09-29

Prisma now converts an Astromesh agent into GCP's own native agent, wired to GCP's base
resources. Still nothing is provisioned for real: the gateway is in-memory.

### Added

- **The native agent.** An Agent becomes an ADK agent config that Agent Engine deploys
  declaratively (`spec.sourceCodeSpec.agentConfigSource.adkConfig.jsonConfig`), verified against
  the `aiplatform` v1 discovery document (revision 20260920) and `google-adk` 2.10.0:
  instruction, model, sampling settings, tools, Model Armor, memory. `pipeline` becomes a
  `SequentialAgent` with one sub-agent per stage.
- **Base resources by binding.** References to resources whose full name only exists after they
  are created are `prisma://{kind}/{manifest}/{resource_type}/{name}` bindings: the RAG Engine
  corpus of the pipeline named in `knowledge`, and the agent's Model Armor template.
- **`prisma_tools.py`**, shipped next to the config: client tools (long-running, the caller
  answers), RAG retrieval, and the callback that writes each turn to Memory Bank. ADK's generic
  config loader cannot build the first two (it drops a `dict` argument, and raises on
  `VertexAiRagRetrieval`).
- **`POST /v1/translate`**: what a manifest becomes, with structured gaps, without storing or
  reconciling it.
- **`tests/test_upstream_contract.py`**: every key of the core's `agent.schema.json` (copied from
  core 0.61.0) must reach the native agent or name the section that reports it.
- A test that **runs** the generated agent in ADK with a recording model and asserts the request
  it sends.

### Changed

- Tools re-grounded on the six types the core loads (`builtin, agent, client, integration, api,
  mcp`): `tools.client`, `tools.builtin.grounded`, `tools.builtin.unmapped`, `tools.agent`,
  `tools.catalog`, `tools.unloadable`, `tools.rate_limit`, `tools.other`, plus `knowledge`.
  A tool with no `type` (`internal`) is no longer reported as supported.
- Client tool `parameters` are normalized exactly like the core (YAML shorthand → JSON Schema).
- Gemini is recognized the way the core reaches it: litellm `vertex_ai/gemini-…` and
  `gemini/gemini-…`. The spec model accepts `source`, the role schema (`default`/`roles`),
  sampling keys and connection keys.
- Memory: conversational memory is the engine's Sessions, semantic memory its Memory Bank (read
  by `preload_memory`, written after every turn). The standalone `vertex.memory_bank` and the
  Vector Search index/endpoint for semantic memory are gone.
- Honest coverage where it lied: `pii_detection` is partial (Model Armor blocks where Astromesh
  redacts), `model.fallback`/`model.routing` are unsupported (one model per native agent),
  `memory.episodic` is unsupported, orchestration no longer says "emulated by Prisma".
- New sections for what used to drop silently: `spec.other`, `identity.other`,
  `model.parameters`, `orchestration.limits`, `guardrails.content_filter`,
  `guardrails.topic_filter`, `guardrails.pii_behavior`; conversational tuning and semantic
  `similarity_threshold`/`max_results` are reported.

### Fixed

- A prompt with Jinja braces is sent as `static_instruction` (literal) instead of an
  `instruction` ADK would fail to template on every call.
- `web_search` is declared in ADK's multi-tool form, so it can share a request with other tools;
  on a non-Gemini model it is reported unsupported instead of failing every turn.
- Model Armor is wired only on the side the rule is declared on, and the template no longer
  enables filters the manifest did not ask for.
- ADK agent names: `user` (reserved by ADK) and names starting with a digit are made valid.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-07-20

First tagged baseline. Everything below already existed on `develop`; this
release exists so the state has a name that can be cited, diffed against, and
rolled back to. **It is a baseline, not a usable product** — read "Known
limitations" before assuming otherwise.

### Added

- **The translation core.** `CloudProvider` (Protocol, plugin boundary), the
  **Homolog Mapping Registry** — one registry of `section -> mapper` that is the
  single source of truth for BOTH provisioning and the generated coverage
  docs, so the matrix cannot drift from the code — a `ManifestRouter` that
  dispatches on `manifest.kind`, and a reconcile loop (observe → diff → apply)
  that is idempotent.
- **Two first-class manifest kinds**, `Agent` and `RAGPipeline`, keyed by
  `(kind, name)`. The provider partitions on `f"{kind}/{name}"`, so an Agent
  and a RAGPipeline sharing a name no longer overwrite each other.
- **A GCP provider mapped onto the researched real surface.** The resources it
  emits are ones that actually exist and are actually creatable:
  `gcp.agent_engine`, `gcp.memory_bank`, `gcp.vector_index`,
  `gcp.vector_index_endpoint`, `gcp.rag_corpus`, `modelarmor.template`.
- **A generated coverage matrix** (`docs/COVERAGE.md`, via
  `scripts/gen_coverage.py`) with 25 rows across four statuses —
  `supported` / `partial` / `emulated` / `unsupported`. Gaps are named, not
  hidden.
- **A FastAPI control surface**: `/v1/specs/{kind}/{name}` and
  `/v1/specs/{kind}/{name}/reconcile`.
- Structural guard tests that fail if a spec field can be dropped without
  producing a coverage gap.

### Known limitations

These are properties of this release, not bugs filed against it:

- **Nothing is provisioned in real GCP.** `GcpApiGateway` is an explicit stub
  and the working gateway is `InMemoryGcpGateway`. Prisma today translates
  specs and reports coverage; it does not deploy. The real gateway is
  "Delivery 2", whose original scope is recorded in `docs/STATUS.md` as
  **out of date** — research since showed `reasoningEngine` has no tools field,
  so real deployment requires Prisma to generate a source package, work that
  scope never described.
- **The tools rows of the coverage matrix are wrong, knowingly.** They were
  built against a tool-type list Astromesh never had
  (`internal|mcp|webhook|agent|rag`); the real YAML-loadable types are
  `builtin | agent | client`. The load-bearing case: `internal` is the default
  for a tool declared without a `type`, Astromesh cannot load it, and this
  release reports it **`supported`** — the matrix lies on its most common row.
  The fix is fully specified and planned (spec + 7-task plan, no decisions
  pending, no GCP credentials needed); it is deliberately not in this tag so
  the baseline reflects what was actually built and reviewed.
- Azure and AWS providers do not exist. The `[aws]` and `[azure]` extras are
  empty placeholders.
